title: customer-support-success
universal_lens: The operational lifecycle of customer support is formalized as a constrained state-transition system. We define a readiness manifold where launch viability requires the simultaneous satisfaction of compliance, testing, and data-verification constraints. The transition from an unknown implementation state to a verified production deployment acts as a projection operator onto a stable subspace.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, the 'unknown implementation state' (Quote 3) represents high epistemic entropy. We apply conformal inference to bound the uncertainty of unverified P0 data. The readiness scorecard functions as a Bayesian posterior update mechanism, continuously refining the probability distribution of launch success based on incoming test evidence and QA verification metrics.
gse_mapping: GSE models this department as a dynamic control loop managing trust and risk reduction. The 'Definition of Ready' and 'Definition of Done' act as strict boundary conditions for valid state transitions. Escalation rules (Quote 12) serve as immediate interrupt vectors, forcing a hard reset to a safe baseline state upon detecting critical anomalies in live affiliate or payment systems.

primitives.assumptions: Assumes all blockers are independent variables contributing linearly to the degradation of the readiness score.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur when blocker count > 0 for P0 items, causing the readiness score to collapse to zero immediately.

primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Escalation Rules Escalate legal/compliance, deploy, production data, payments, live affiliate, method leakage, or P0 data accuracy problems immediately.

layer2.telemetry: Frequency and resolution time of P0 escalations logged in the master build queue.

The mathematical foundation of this department rests on the rigorous management of state transitions under uncertainty. We begin by defining the system state vector \mathbf{X}, which encompasses all UI routes, backend configurations, and compliance flags. Quote 3 explicitly establishes that the initial condition \mathbf{X}_0 is characterized by maximum epistemic entropy; we simply do not know what is deployed. To navigate this, we introduce the Readiness Projection Operator \Pi_R (derived from Quote 7). This operator maps the high-dimensional, uncertain state space onto a lower-dimensional manifold of 'launch-ready' configurations. A state \mathbf{X} is only valid if \Pi_R(\mathbf{X}) = 1, which mathematically necessitates that the blocker count B equals zero and the test evidence set E is complete. The 'Definition of Ready' (Quote 10) and 'Definition of Done' (Quote 11) act as strict topological boundaries, ensuring that any trajectory through the state space does not cross into undefined or unverified regions. Furthermore, the system is subject to external shocks—specifically, P0 data inaccuracies or compliance breaches. These are modeled as Critical Escalation Interrupt Vectors \mathbf{I}_{crit} (Quote 12). When \mathbf{I}_{crit} is triggered, it imposes a hard constraint, instantly freezing the state evolution and requiring a rollback to a known safe subspace. The interplay between reducing the entropy of the implementation state (via real app clone verification) and maintaining a robust projection onto the readiness manifold forms the core dynamical equation of this primitive. Failure modes arise when the rate of state mutation (new builds) outpaces the rate of entropy reduction (QA/testing), leading to a systemic collapse of the readiness score.
